source.title: Singularity-Induced Local Complexity for High-Dimensional Learning Models

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses generalization and sharpness, but its results concern theoretical bounds and the relation between local RLCT and Hessian rank. It does not measure the training–test gap or test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior sharpness and generalization results, but does not reproduce them. Its own experiment compares Hessian eigenvalues with local RLCT; these comparisons do not measure the training–test gap required by the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study proves local RLCT bounds and compares local RLCT with Hessian spectra at constructed minimizers. These results do not test V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation measure or its empirical association with generalization gaps, and do not bear on V1–V6 or V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. Precisely, the authors prove rank(Hessian) ≤ 2λ at local minimizers under analyticity, derive a local covering-number bound and a conditional local uniform generalization-gap bound, and interpret local RLCT as partially capturing effective dimension or intrinsic complexity.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops theoretical bounds and checks a Hessian-rank inequality numerically; it does not reproduce the original studies' interventions or train/test-gap measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the Hessian-rank comparison is unclear for ReLU networks, whose activation is non-analytic; GELU comparisons are described as approximate and fluctuating.

fits_no_version.finding: The simple-model calculations and numerical comparisons satisfy Hessian rank ≤ twice local RLCT at the displayed minimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For analytic population risks, twice the local RLCT upper-bounds Hessian rank at local minimizers.

fits_no_version.finding: GELU comparisons approximately bound the number of dominant Hessian eigenvalues by twice estimated local RLCT; ReLU comparisons are inconclusive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Estimated local RLCT can characterize dominant Hessian directions, with evidence depending on analyticity and estimation.

fits_no_version.finding: The study derives local covering-number and uniform generalization-gap upper bounds under realizability, analyticity, and a covariance condition near population-risk global minimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local RLCT enters conditional upper bounds on local model complexity and generalization gaps.

record.problems: The general-network experiments estimate local RLCT with an SGLD-based procedure and describe the Hessian eigenvalues as difficult to classify because they decay gradually. The ReLU experiments do not clearly support the theorem's claim. No train/test gap is measured.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant rows left out; the reported experiments are represented, but they do not map to any listed claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under random versus natural labels.
Held-out error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected classification performance and the role of local connectivity.
Optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data and regularization regimes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, empirical gap rankings, and comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Held-out accuracy after removing memorized versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Population risk is called generalization error in this paper; computing its Hessian does not measure a training–test gap. The theoretical gap bounds concern local RLCT, a different quantity from V7's magnitude-aware sharpness, and establish no empirical ranking of gaps.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Test error across widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification.
Generalization comparisons among adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers.
Generalization comparisons across batch sizes and training recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its association with the training–test gap.
Effect on held-out accuracy of removing memorized examples.

rows.subject: reduced-rank regression
rows.operation_detail: Compared Hessian rank at three global minimizers with twice the local RLCT.
rows.value: rank ∇2 R(wi) ≤ 2λ(wi) (i=1,2,3) holds; at w3, local RLCT differs from Hessian rank.
rows.note: This tests the paper's Hessian-rank bound, not a training–test gap.
rows.check: The Hessian-rank comparison measures none of the listed effects. Its observed state describes the paper's own inequality.

rows.subject: linear neural network
rows.operation_detail: Compared Hessian rank at three global minimizers with twice the local RLCT.
rows.note: This tests the paper's Hessian-rank bound, not a training–test gap.
rows.check: The Hessian-rank comparison measures none of the listed effects. Section 5.1 also reports λ(w1)=1/2, whereas equation (5) and the stated dimensions imply λ(w1)=1; the source is internally inconsistent.

rows.subject: GELU network
rows.operation_detail: Compared Hessian eigenvalues with estimated local RLCT at five parameters representing the zero function.
rows.measure: Dominant Hessian eigenvalues relative to estimated local RLCT
rows.value: Results suggest the local RLCT roughly upper-bounds the number of large eigenvalues, despite fluctuations.
rows.note: The authors describe the result as approximate; no training–test gap is measured.
rows.check: This compares Hessian eigenvalues with twice the estimated local RLCT, not magnitude-aware sharpness with generalization gaps. The value should specify the factor of two.
